text:
Jordan: Hey team — noticed a weird divergence between `kv_hit_rate` and observed tail latency for long-context requests. Hit rate metric looks flat around 92% but `kv_residency` shows steady memory growth during our 20k-token load tests. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

Sam: Yep, saw node-3 alerts last night. Memory on that host trended up even after traffic subsided. My hunch: hit rate calc is sampling only successful full-key lookups, which hides partial-prefix reuse and fragmentation.

Maria: Which dashboard are you looking at?

Jordan: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/kv-cache/kv-cache-overview?orgId=1 — check the "residency" and "live entries" panels. The weird part is residency% keeps creeping while evictions counter stays low.

Kevin: Could be fragmentation. Runtime allocs show many tiny KV chunks that leave holes when entries rotate. We currently expose `kv_live_entries` but not fragmentation bytes per shard. That would explain increasing RSS without proportional eviction counts.

profiler-bot: profiler snapshot (top lines):
```
heap_profile: 2026-02-14T03:20:45Z
total_allocated_bytes: 14.2GB
kv_pool_used: 9.6GB
kv_frag_bytes: 1.9GB
top_hot_prefixes:
  chat:usr: -> entries=342, avg_entry=10kb, last_used=38s
  instruct: -> entries=120, avg_entry=64kb, last_used=6s
  system: -> entries=58, avg_entry=128kb, last_used=2h
```

Anya: Quick checklist we should add asap: 1) eviction counters per shard 2) `kv_frag_bytes` metric 3) windowed/request-weighted hit rate so single large models don't skew global hit rate.

Jordan: Example PromQL for windowed hit rate we can add to dashboard:
```
# request-weighted 5m hit rate
sum(increase(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(increase(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
```
And residency percent:
```
(kv_cache_live_entries_total / kv_cache_capacity_entries) * 100
```

Sam: Also add `kv_cache_partial_hits_total` — we currently count only exact-key hits. Prefix reuse (partial kv) results in model-level speedups but not being captured. That inflates perceived hit rate vs effective token-level benefit.

Kevin: There's a timeline correlation with the kernel-selection change we rolled 2026-02-14 03:12Z — batching heuristics changed how sequences are chunked and that likely increased long-lived prefix reuse for a subset of traffic, increasing residency. Need to correlate deploy time with `kv_residency` spike.

Anya: Suggested alert rule: if `kv_residency_percent > 80` for 10m AND `rate(kv_evictions_total[5m]) < 1` -> fire. Means we're running out of room but not evicting (likely fragmentation or a bug blocking eviction).

ops-bot: Created INF-4321: "kv cache metrics + shard eviction counters" and assigned to @Jordan and @Kevin.

Jordan: I'll prototype emitting `kv_frag_bytes`, `kv_evictions_total{shard=...}`, and `kv_partial_hits_total`. Will instrument per-shard labels and include `model` tag. Posting PR soon.

Sam: When you add metrics, include Prometheus histogram for eviction latency (how long entries survive before eviction) and a per-shard heatmap panel.

Maria: Once metrics ship, I'll update Grafana: panels to add -> "Evictions by shard (heatmap)", "Fragmentation bytes", "Hit rate (5m/1h weighted)", "Residency by model/kernel". Also add links to the code that emits metrics in the panel description.

Jordan: Quick debug command I used to inspect problematic entries:
```
# quick inspection tool (internal)
./bin/kv-inspect --host node-3 --top 20 --sort frag_bytes
# sample output
shard=5 prefix='chat:usr:123' frag_bytes=12MB entries=240 last_used_seconds=202
shard=2 prefix='instruct:img-gen' frag_bytes=8MB entries=46 last_used_seconds=34
```

Kevin: Good. Also add unit and integration tests to ensure eviction counters increment on eviction, and that `kv_frag_bytes` decreases when compaction runs.

Anya: Long-term: consider switching to a segmented-LRU with compaction pass or reuse-aware allocation to reduce fragmentation for very long contexts. Also explore TTL by prefix class for chat vs system prefixes.

Jordan: Will follow up with PR + dashboard mock. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Noted and added to release checklist for next runtime patch."
